title: Exploring NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning: Making it see with little resources
gist: German consultancy TNG grafted vision onto the text-only NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model by freezing an existing vision encoder (Kimi K2.6 Vision Tower or NVIDIA C-Radiov4-H) and training only a small MLP projector — 34-40 million parameters on roughly 100 million tokens, run on entry-level RTX 6000 Pro GPUs in a few days. The result reached usable MMMU scores and lifted medical VQA validation accuracy from 20% to 58%, and Nemotron's hybrid Mamba architecture delivered 50% higher fine-tuning token throughput than Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B.

insights.claim: Vision can be added to a text-only LLM by fully reusing an existing pretrained vision encoder and training only a small MLP adapter, because capable encoders already exist and merely operate in a different embedding space than the target model.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Multimodality is becoming a cheap bolt-on rather than a training-run moat, eroding the differentiation of vendors selling 'natively multimodal' frontier models.
insights.quote: the essential idea is not to train an entire vision encoder, but fully re-use an existing one and only train the absolute bare minimum: a small MLP adapter
insights.locator: In separate experiments, we injected both

insights.claim: Only the final projection layer of a vision encoder needs adaptation to a new host LLM, since that projection is the sole component translating the encoder's representation into the target model's embedding space.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Implies vision encoders are effectively commodity, portable modules — value accrues to whoever owns the encoder weights, not the integration.
insights.quote: This suggests that only the final projection in an existing vision encoder requires adaptation, namely the one that translates the encoder's representation into the target LLM's embedding space.

insights.claim: TNG's approach adapts a recipe demonstrated by GLM-5.2 Vision, which showed that a vision tower such as Kimi K2.6 can be injected into a separate LLM like GLM-5.2 with minimal training.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Cross-vendor component mixing (Chinese vision towers into US open-weight LLMs) is now routine, undermining assumptions about model-family lock-in.
insights.quote: GLM-5.2 Vision demonstrated how a Vision Tower like Kimi K2.6 can be injected into an LLM like GLM-5.2 with minimal training.
insights.locator: Instead, we decided to go for a simplified approach

insights.claim: The full multimodal recipe NVIDIA published with Nemotron 3 Nano Omni requires several training phases on hundreds of billions of tokens, which TNG deliberately bypassed as infeasible for a small proof of concept.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Quantifies the gap between vendor-grade and shortcut multimodality — roughly three orders of magnitude in training tokens — which is where the quality delta shows up.
insights.quote: which would have required several training phases on hundreds of billions of tokens
insights.locator: How to get Vision Capabilities into a Non-Vision LLM on the cheap

insights.claim: TNG trained only 34 million parameters using the Kimi K2.6 tower and 40 million using NVIDIA C-Radiov4-H, versus the hundreds of millions of parameters a conventional approach would require.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude reduction in trainable parameters puts custom multimodal models inside the budget of mid-sized enterprises, not just labs.
insights.quote: only 34 million (Kimi K2.6) - 40 million (NVIDIA C-Radiov4-H) parameters instead of hundreds of millions of parameters needed to be trained
insights.locator: For our experiments, only part 4) of the image pipeline

insights.claim: The entire vision-grafting training run consumed only around 100 million tokens, a training budget several orders of magnitude below a standard multimodal pretraining pipeline.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Data-scale requirements collapse when only the projector is trained, removing the data-moat argument for multimodal capability.
insights.quote: Our train runs used around 100 million tokens.
insights.locator: For our experiments, only part 4) of the image pipeline

insights.claim: The fine-tuning would have been feasible on a single entry-level server GPU (RTX 6000 Pro); TNG used eight only to shorten wall-clock time via data parallelism.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Customisation demand is shifting toward workstation-class and entry server GPUs, broadening NVIDIA's addressable base below the H100/GB200 tier.
insights.quote: While fine-tuning would be feasible on a single GPU, we used 8 for faster training times through data parallelism.

insights.claim: The whole vision extension took a few days of tinkering and a couple of GPU hours, per TNG's own account of the effort involved.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Time-to-capability for a bespoke multimodal model is now days, not quarters — compressing the window in which any model capability stays proprietary.
insights.quote: With just a few days of tinkering and a couple of GPU hours we were able to extend it with fundamental vision capabilities

insights.claim: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning delivered 50% higher token throughput than Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B during a comparative fine-tune, a direct efficiency advantage measured on identical work.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: A 50% throughput edge translates directly into lower cost per customised model, a concrete reason for self-hosters to pick Nemotron over Qwen.
insights.quote: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning had a 50% higher token throughput compared to Qwen during fine-tuning.
insights.locator: For comparison, we also ran a comparative fine-tune

insights.claim: TNG's benchmarking confirmed that Nemotron 3.5 Lightning's hybrid Mamba architecture translates into real measured efficiency rather than a paper claim.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Independent validation of state-space/attention hybrids strengthens the case that pure-transformer inference economics are being undercut.
insights.quote: we found it to be a highly efficient model and indeed observed the hybrid Mamba architecture paying off
insights.locator: We were thrilled to get an early-access version

insights.claim: High training efficiency, not raw benchmark scores, is what TNG identifies as the property making Nemotron 3.5 Lightning particularly well suited to customisation via fine-tuning.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Reframes open-weight model selection around fine-tune cost rather than leaderboard position — a different buying criterion than the one most model marketing targets.
insights.quote: particularly well suited for customization via fine-tuning due to its high training efficiency

insights.claim: Visual grounding emerged progressively across the projector training run: at step 500 the model hallucinated Bitcoin, at 1000 the Linux Foundation, at 2000 Intel and NVIDIA, at 3000 TNT and NVIDIA, and only at step 4000 correctly identified the TNG and NVIDIA logos.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Shows how few optimisation steps separate confident hallucination from correct grounding — a caution for anyone evaluating early multimodal checkpoints.
insights.quote: ranging from pure hallucination at the beginning to a pretty good understanding at step 4000

insights.claim: The cheaply grafted vision model scored below NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni on the MMMU benchmark, confirming that shortcut multimodality trades measurable capability for cost.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: The gap defines where full vendor training still earns its cost — general-purpose vision — versus where a projector graft suffices.
insights.quote: While falling short of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni scores, we find those results very convincing given how little time for training and data preparation was invested on our side.

insights.claim: For the medical imaging use case TNG went beyond the projector and full fine-tuned the entire vision encoder, indicating domain specialisation requires touching more of the stack than cross-modal alignment does.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: A two-tier customisation ladder: cheap projector training for modality, heavier encoder training for domain — different cost profiles for different enterprise asks.
insights.quote: we decided to do a full fine-tune of the vision encoder (i.e. all parts 1 - 4 in Figure 1) to enhance its capabilities in the medical domain
insights.locator: As an example use case for adding vision capabilities

insights.claim: Fine-tuning on a comparatively small number of medical images lifted validation accuracy on the imageclef-medical-vqa-2019 task from 20% to 58%, nearly tripling performance.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Domain fine-tuning on modest datasets closes most of the gap to specialised medical AI vendors, compressing that category's defensibility.
insights.quote: we observed a significant improvement of the answers on our validation dataset from 20% to 58%
insights.locator: As an example use case for adding vision capabilities

themes.theme: European sovereign inference as a business

insights.claim: TNG is a 930-employee Munich software consultancy operating more than 250 GPUs in service and serving over 10 billion tokens per day from inference endpoints hosted inside Germany.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: A consultancy-scale operator running 10B tokens/day shows sovereign European inference is a real, revenue-bearing niche — not just policy rhetoric.
insights.quote: We provide LLM inference in Europe with currently more than 250 GPUs in service. Our inference endpoints serve more than 10 billion tokens per day.
insights.locator: For context, TNG is a software consultancy

insights.claim: TNG's commercial differentiation rests on data governance rather than model quality: zero data retention, a no-log policy, a highly secured German cluster and hardware-based Confidential Computing for stricter requirements.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Confirms the enterprise wedge for open-weight hosting is compliance and data residency, a segment US hyperscaler APIs structurally cannot serve.
insights.quote: Our models are hosted in a highly secured cluster with zero data retention, a no-log policy and served from within Germany.
insights.locator: For context, TNG is a software consultancy

insights.claim: TNG hosts a rotating roster of the latest open-weight models including Kimi K3, GLM 5.2 and Nemotron variants, screening each through an internal benchmark suite before deployment.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Self-hosters treat open-weight models as interchangeable inventory, so model vendors face near-zero switching costs at this layer of the market.
insights.quote: We host the latest open-weight models available, such as Kimi K3, GLM 5.2 and the latest Nemotron variants.
insights.locator: For context, TNG is a software consultancy

insights.claim: Open-weight models are valuable to businesses on two distinct axes — cost-efficient self-hosted inference and substantial customisation — with TNG's own research arm producing merged and post-trained models more token-efficient than their parents.
insights.speaker: Fabian Klemm
insights.so_what: Derivative models built by integrators expand the open-weight ecosystem's effective capability without any vendor spend, further pressuring closed-API pricing.
insights.quote: Open-weight models such as NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning allow cost-efficient, self-hosted inference for small and large businesses while also allowing for substantial customization.
insights.locator: Open-weight models such as NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
